assumptions.text: Q-1 (non-blocking, no answers file present) asks whether whitespace-trimming of the username should be part of the tested contract. Login.jsx currently does username.trim().toLowerCase() before comparison, so leading/trailing whitespace in the username currently succeeds when paired with the correct password. Absent an authoritative answer, this plan tests the implemented behavior as-is (SC-6/EC-1) rather than assuming it should be rejected, and separately verifies the password side is NOT trimmed (SC-7/EC-2), so the asymmetry is captured either way Q-1 is eventually resolved.

Q-2 (non-blocking, no answers file present) asks whether a check confirming /login does not link to /login-broken should be planned. This plan includes it (SC-13/EC-5) as a low-cost regression guard against future accidental conflation of the working /login flow and the CAP-18 simulated-outage page, without asserting anything about /login-broken's own behavior (which remains out of scope per AC-7/REQ-12).

All locators in this plan (getByLabel('Card number or username'), getByLabel('Password', exact), getByRole('button', {name:'Sign On'}), getByRole('alert'), the Forgot password/Register links, and the Remember this device checkbox) were verified directly against C:\Users\sumit.kumar1\Documents\bank-app-1\src\pages\Login.jsx source, not inferred from any graph/architecture tool — this ticket's scope is a single self-contained page component with no cross-component relationship question, so no Helix query was needed or used for structural planning.

outOfScope.reason: Marked testable: false in the baseline — the 'Remember this device' checkbox is decorative only, with no persisted behavior to verify. SC-12 exercises REQ-11 (the checkbox can be checked/unchecked) but asserts no persisted state, per the baseline's own scoping.

Marked testable: false in the baseline — the /login-broken simulated-outage page belongs to CAP-18 and must not be conflated with /login's own test coverage. REQ-12 and EC-5 are covered by SC-13, which only confirms /login does not link to /login-broken; no assertions are made about /login-broken's own behavior.
